joekray-mond.name: Joekray Mond (Joe K. Raymond)

rounds.question: Great, good or gruesome on the decade — and does the 2026 break change the verdict or only the price?
rounds.conclusion: 华特达因 is a great business on its decade that broke in 2026 for reasons the local record cannot show. Its pediatric-pharma subsidiary nearly tripled operating profit after tax (3.69亿 FY2016 → 9.96亿 FY2025) while net operating assets shrank (12.21亿 → 8.55亿), and free cash flow (66.07亿) matched total profit (67.97亿) over ten years; about half of the capital release was operating liabilities that reversed in 2026 (6.36亿 → 2.84亿). In 2026, 9M revenue fell 45%, Q3 revenue (0.33亿) came in below its cost of sales, and operating cash flow turned negative (−3.32亿). At 43.52亿 (S1 quote 2026-11-20, 18.57元) the price is not betting on a return to 2025. Valuing the parent's cash at face (central estimate about 17.9亿 of parent net financial assets, assuming minorities own their 48% profit share of a subsidiary holding all operations; limits 10.8–21.7亿), it asks the roughly 26亿 operating stake for about 2.6亿 a year at a 10% hurdle (2.1亿 at 8%, 3.1亿 at 12%). That is about the trailing parent profit of 2.8亿, but that year still holds three pre-break quarters and Q3 alone lost 0.67亿, so the price bets that Q3 was a one-off; FY2025 parent operating profit was at least 5.0亿. The insight to remember: the decisive questions are measurement and cause, not the multiple. Revenue looks booked net of rebates paid back in cash (from 2020 to 2025 the excess of cash collected over revenue grew 8.8亿 while other operating cash paid grew 7.9亿; VAT and expense growth explain only part — a hypothesis until the notes are read), so a single accrual can swing a whole quarter. The panel passes until the 2026 Q3 report names the cause. Scorecard: business type GREAT on the decade (operating profit ×2.7 while gross operating assets also fell, 16.8 → 14.9亿; the consolidated gross-margin climb from 60.9% to 85.1% is the exit from low-margin side businesses, the pharma segment held near 84%); cash backing YES through FY2025 (FCF/NI 0.97; capex front-loaded in 2016–19, recent capex below depreciation), NO in 2026 (9M operating cash −3.32亿 while 9.73亿 of dividends went out); return driver MARGIN on an almost capital-free operation (RNOA 102% in FY2025 = margin 44.7% × turnover 2.29, partly levered by operating-liability float), with the parent's ROE (18.7%) diluted by a cash pile and by minorities taking 46.9% of the decade's profit; cheap or not CHEAP on FY2025 (12.3% earnings yield), FAIR on the trailing year (6.5%) and not cheap on the Q3 run-rate; floor PARTIAL: about two-fifths of the price in parent net financial assets at book (central case), a quarter to a half at the limits. Capital allocation: 64% of the decade's parent profit was declared as dividends, FY2024–25 payouts exceeded profit (114%, 110%); no raises or buybacks. Confidence medium: the business verdict rests on direct S2 series, but the valuation depends on an argued hurdle, an estimated ownership split, unverified rebate mechanics, and documents not in the local data.

rounds.question: Gruesome on the full decade: is the 3,836亿 of net operating assets still earning anything, or is the book just carrying it at cost?
rounds.conclusion: Vanke was a gruesome business dressed as a great one. For a decade homebuyers' deposits and suppliers funded the growth, so ROE ran near 20% while operations produced no free cash: ten-year operating income after tax of 2,055亿 against Penman free cash flow (OI − ΔNOA) of −273亿 (same total-firm scope; parent profit 825亿), with net operating assets nearly tripling to 2023. Since 2021 the float has run in reverse — customer deposits down 89%, mostly settled by delivering homes — and selling down the land bank left almost no cash (FY2022–25 operating cash 95亿); in 2026 sales lose money once sales taxes and interest are paid. At 336亿 (S1 quote 2026-11-20, 2.82元) the stock is 0.36× parent book, but the book is not a floor: the equity is 7.9% of a 4,245亿 enterprise (each 1% on enterprise value moves the stock about 12.6%), tangible book of 554亿 falls to the price with a write-down averaging under 3% on the remaining non-cash assets and to zero at about 6.6%, and 1,898亿 of debt falls due within a year against 524亿 of cash. The price asks for about 40亿 a year of steady profit at the argued 12% hurdle (27亿 at 8%, 50亿 at 15%) against losses near 80亿 a quarter. The insight to remember: this is no longer an earnings question but a bet on asset realization and on who rolls the debt — a speculation the local record cannot underwrite, so the panel passes for now. Scorecard: business type GRUESOME on the full cycle (capital-hungry growth, then losses; OI core pretax 835亿 in 2020 to a loss in FY2025); cash backing NO — CFO 2,544亿 in FY2016–20 rode the deposit float, FY2021–23 CFO was 108亿 against 573亿 of parent profit, and CFO − capex (2,057亿) overstates owner cash because land sits in CFO and JV stakes in investing (CFO + investing 534亿); return driver LEVERAGE — asset turnover 0.2–0.3 and a 6–10× equity multiplier, with the leverage hidden in operating liabilities (2.77× NOA in 2021); capital allocation: 761亿 of dividends declared FY2016–22 against 368亿 of operating and investing cash in the same years, with partners' capital (1,335亿) and debt filling the gap; cheap or not CHEAP TO BOOK ONLY (PB 0.36, earnings and after-interest cash negative); floor NONE for the equity — tangible book ex deferred tax assets 554亿 is above the price but shrinks about 80亿 a quarter and vanishes with a write-down averaging about 6.6% on the remaining non-cash assets (parent bearing all of it, labelled). Confidence medium: the business verdict rests on direct S2 series, but the valuation pass depends on an argued hurdle and on annual-report notes not in the local data.

rounds.question: Is 云铝股份 a good business now that growth stopped needing capital — and is 21.01 yuan cheap on normalized, mid-cycle earnings rather than on the 2026 peak?
rounds.conclusion: 云铝股份 is a good, harvest-phase commodity business, not a great franchise. The decade splits in two: a gruesome 2016–2020 build-out (7亿 parent profit on 167亿 capex, three placements totaling ~87亿, shares +33%) and a 2021–2025 harvest (223亿 profit on 43亿 capex, net debt of 134亿 turned into net cash of 212亿). The 2026 profit spike (9M parent 116亿; gross margin 10%→32% in four quarters) is cost-driven — revenue +19% while cost of sales fell 4% — consistent with an alumina-price-collapse hypothesis, and the market knows it: the stock fell 36% YTD to 21.01 even as TTM earnings tripled. So PE(TTM) 5.5 and a 21% FCF yield are peak mirages; on mid-cycle profit of 55–60亿 the price is 12–13×, implying ~1% perpetual growth at an 8% hurdle (zero-growth return 7.5–8.2%), with net cash equal to 29% of market cap as cushion and an asset floor near 36% of cap. Verdict: reasonably cheap on normalized earnings, not on peak; the reader should remember that the price already pays for the bust, not the boom. The swing facts are alumina-price persistence and whether the 232亿 cash hoard reaches owners. Scorecard: business type — good in harvest, commodity spread not franchise; cash backing — 10y FCF 261亿 = 1.13× parent NI, but current FCF overstates owner cash if maintenance ≈ D&A; return driver — margin 0.7%→10.1% and turnover 0.49→1.36 on a shrinking base, leverage gone (multiplier 3.5→1.4); cheap/floor — priced at mid-cycle no-growth, floor ~264亿 protects about a third. Confidence: medium (normalized-earnings assumptions, 25% tax default, unverified controller/related-party facts, no local commodity price series).

rounds.question: Is the harvest's free cash real owner cash, and what normal earning power should today's price be tested against?
rounds.conclusion: Yunnan Aluminium is a good business in harvest, not a great one: a cost-position commodity smelter whose decade splits into a capital-hungry build-out (FY2016-20 parent profit 6.99亿 on capex 167.3亿) and a cash-rich harvest (FY2021-25 profit 223.1亿, free cash 308.6亿). The decade's cash backs the profit (10y FCF 260.8亿 = 1.13x parent NI 230.1亿), but harvest capex at 0.47x depreciation means today's free cash overstates owner cash unless maintenance is genuinely cheap. At 728.6亿 (S1 quote 2026-11-20, 21.01元) the price is not buying the 2026 peak: on the mechanical harvest median 44.1亿 it pays 6.1% with no growth and needs 4.6% perpetual growth at an 8% hurdle; stripping the 211.8亿 hoard and its assumed carry, the operating business yields about 7.9% with no growth, or about 7.7% once minorities' book share of the cash is deducted — at or below the hurdle, not above it. The insight to remember: the market's 36% fall against trailing profit up ~166% is a bet that the cost-side windfall reverses, and the price already sits at mid-cycle no-growth, so the upside depends on alumina persistence or the hoard reaching owners, not on the boom continuing. Scorecard: business type GOOD in harvest (commodity spread, no franchise moat); cash backing YES over the decade (1.13x) but current FCF flattered by deferred maintenance; return driver margin and turnover up on a growing base over FY2016-25 (RNOA 5.0% to 28.6%, NOA 170.5亿 to 254.3亿), with base shrinkage (291.6亿 to 254.3亿) only in FY2021-25; leverage gone; cheap or not FAIR at mid-cycle no-growth — the ex-cash operating yield meets the 8% hurdle only at the mid band and only on the consolidated-cash basis; floor about 272亿 (37% of cap) with stated haircuts protects roughly a third of the price. Confidence medium: the mid-cycle base is mechanical, the carry yield and maintenance (c) are labelled assumptions, and the bear case is unrefuted locally.

rounds.question: After eight years of 28% yearly growth, sales growth fell to under 1% in Q3 2026. Is this a pause or the end, and what does the price at 113.55 yuan assume?
rounds.conclusion: The business looks like a strong franchise whose easy growth is fading, and the price already sits at a sensible midpoint. Sales grew 28% a year for eight years on almost no capital, with cash flow above profit. This year growth fell to under 1%, and 2025's growth already came more from thinner-margin products than from the flagship energy drink. At 113.55 yuan the operating business is priced at about 15 times its core profit. That needs only 1.4 to 4.2% a year of lasting profit growth, depending on whether dealers' prepayments count as debt and on whether investors want 8% or 10%. So the price does not assume growth is over, and it is not assuming strong growth either. If growth really ended, the market value would fall roughly 14 to 34%. Whether this is a pause or the end is not answerable from the data in hand. Fourth-quarter sales and the year-end prepayment build will decide it. Confidence: medium on the price-implied part, low on pause versus end.

rounds.question: The H1 2026 product split is now in the local data. Where is growth actually coming from, and is the record gross margin pricing power or a cost windfall?
rounds.conclusion: The 2026 stall is a volume and base story, not a price war, and the record profit margin is a cost windfall that masks a mix shift toward thinner-margin drinks. The flagship energy drink still grew about 7% in the first half, but the electrolyte second curve braked from 118% growth last year to 12%, and tea — at roughly 24 cents of gross profit per yuan against 55 for energy — now supplies more than half the sales gain. Every line's margin rose, which rules out a price war and points to cheaper inputs; the energy margin's record 54.7% is borrowed, not earned. Stripping that windfall out of the trailing profit raises the growth the price needs from about 1.4% to about 1.8% at an 8% hurdle — still modest, but the safety margin is thinner than round 1 thought, and the third-quarter margin has already started to fade. The franchise is intact (dealers still prepay, up 43%, and the model needs almost no capital), so this is a maturing franchise priced for modest growth, not a broken business. Whether it is a pause or the end is still not answerable: it turns on fourth-quarter sales, the year-end dealer prepayment build, and whether the gross margin keeps sliding toward 45% while sales stay flat. Confidence: medium on the cost-windfall and mix reading (direct product lines), low on pause versus end.

rounds.question: The company took in about 99 亿 in the first quarter, is still borrowing around 63 亿, and has not obviously spent the money. What was the raise for, and does the 2026 buyback and dividend record show owner-minded capital allocation?
rounds.conclusion: The 2026 capital record is mostly owner-minded but carries one unanswered 99 亿 question. The company raised about 99 亿 in the first quarter at an implied price below last year's close, then parked roughly 55 亿 net in wealth management while plant spending fell about 16%, and in the same nine months declared about 36 亿 of dividends (87% of profit) and bought back about 10 亿 of stock. The confusing second share step was a free bonus issue, not dilution. The borrowing next to the cash pile is a rational positive carry — about 1.4% cost against 2.6%-plus yields — not distress. The raise does not change the operating valuation: the cash is already excluded from the operating enterprise value, parked cash is worth roughly face value, and the growth the price needs stays at the modest ~1.8% at an 8% hurdle. What the raise does is dilute reported return on equity from about 52% to about 34%, which is a growth problem (more cash than the business can absorb at its old return), not a quality problem. Read together with rounds 1 and 2 — cooling growth, a borrowed margin cushion, and now a cash-bloated capital base — this is three independent signs that the easy compounding is over, and the market already prices modest growth rather than the old 28% compounder. The unresolved governance point is the purpose of the raise: the use of proceeds is not in the local data, and an exchange loss hints at possible foreign-currency proceeds. Until the issue announcement is read, management is owner-minded on the evidence available, with a 99 亿 question mark. Confidence: medium on the cash-flow facts and the carry/ROE reading, low on the governance verdict and the carry hypothesis.

Sales grew almost seven times since 2018 with almost no net capital added, because dealers prepay about 60 亿 a year ahead; the return is a margin story, with net margin up from 7% to 21%. Cash backs profit, but about a quarter of eight years of operating cash was dealer float; without it free cash flow was 60% of profit. At 113.55 the operating business is 15 times its after-tax operating profit (a 6.7% yield), which needs only about 1% to 3% perpetual growth on either basis, and book value is no floor: net cash is 17–18% of the price and a conservative floor 15 to 21%, on either balance sheet (FY2025 year-end plus the 99 亿 raise, or September 2026). Before the raise the year-end floor was only about 3% of today's price. Scorecard: business type great with a float caveat; cash backing about 100% with the float and 60% without; return driver margin; cheap only if the franchise lasts; floor 15–21% of price.
